brief: DB previews the week of Sept 28 to Oct 2: August JOLTS Tuesday, ADP (+85k forecast vs +38k prior) Wednesday, jobless claims (200k vs 197k) Thursday, and the September jobs report Friday. DB forecasts +60k headline and +60k private payrolls, both below August's +162k and +127k, with unemployment steady at 4.1% though August's unrounded 4.14% leaves risk it rounds up to 4.2%. Hours worked slip to 34.3 and average hourly earnings rise +0.4%, so aggregate private compensation growth eases to 4.2% from 4.3%. Wednesday's GDP revision (+1.5% vs +2.1%) carries BEA benchmark changes that DB expects to revise July's PCE year-over-year rate down from 3.34% toward 3.0-3.1%, mostly from downward revisions earlier in the window, with slight upward revisions possible to recent prints. Core PCE is forecast at +0.27%. DB expects little new from Fedspeak but flags Thursday's Williams-Cook panel: Cook is seen backing another hike next year, Williams as more dovish, wanting rates back to 3.5-3.75% by 2027's year-end. DB's base case is two more hikes, December and March, with scope for an earlier October hike if data trends persist, and r-star risk adding up to 50bps upside, consistent with about 90bps priced by the forward curve.
